requirement_text.REQ-434:
The feature below cannot be built without first deciding whether it is allowed. This entry is a DESIGN-AND-DECISION requirement: it writes a decision record and a design document, no application code (CODE-DESIGNER is design-only). It is the first entry on purpose, as REQ-384 did with decision 0038 before any code existed.
THE FEATURE (user-approved). A platform-level directory maps a normalised email to the tenants where it has an account. The SPA shows an email-first screen before any redirect: exactly one tenant -> go straight to that tenant's Keycloak realm login with login_hint; several -> tenant choice or emailed list (per the disclosure mode below); none -> neutral outcome. After login, tenant resolution is unchanged: the token's realm -> Letflow.Identity.resolve_tenant_by_realm/1 (lib/letflow/identity.ex:150, decision 0006 R5). ?realm= and host-based resolution (web/src/auth/tenantConfig.ts resolveRealmFromUrl, GET /api/tenant-config) remain as fallbacks/overrides. The in-app tenant switcher (REQ-384, GET /api/v1/me/memberships) is untouched.
DECISIONS THIS ENTRY MUST FLAG AS REQUIRING REVIEWER SIGN-OFF (do not diverge silently; each is a real conflict found by reading the records):
1. Decision 0006 s3.3 / s7 item 3, as already amended by 0038. 0038's 'What remains foreclosed' list names 'a self-service find-my- account(s)-by-email flow reachable by an unauthenticated ... caller' and 'a cross-tenant lookup keyed on anything the caller supplies at request time'. This feature IS that flow. It needs a SECOND, wider, explicitly bounded amendment (0042), not an inference from 0038. The design must state the bounded inference precisely (what an unauthenticated caller can and cannot learn) and why it is accepted, in the manner 0028 states its 'Accepted bounded inference'.
2. Decision 0035 states the SPA has no in-app login surface and no /login route; credentials are entered only on Keycloak's hosted UI. The new email-first page collects an email address, never a credential, and hands off to Keycloak unchanged. 0042 must say that 0035's core decision (credentials are never entered in the SPA) stands and that its 'no /login route' observation is amended to allow a credential-free discovery route.
3. Decision 0028 says Letflow has 'exactly one unauthenticated read surface' (/api/public, handle-addressed) with standing prohibitions: no caller-supplied tenant hint, no collection/search route, no 401/403, and AuthPipeline keeps its no-allowlist property. The lookup here is keyed by a caller-supplied email, so it MUST NOT be mounted under /api/public. The design must decide the mount (recommended: a new sibling forward('/api/login-discovery', ...) on Letflow.Router, declared before the /api/v1 forward, in the manner of /api/tenant-config), and 0042 must state that this does not reopen 0028 (AuthPipeline stays allowlist-free; /api/public stays handle-only) while REVIEWER decides whether 0028's 'exactly one' sentence needs a one-line cross-reference.
4. Decision 0040 concerns AUTHENTICATED routes and defers a general per-actor limiter to S4 (Letflow.Plugs.RateLimit, a deferred row in lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex). It does not cover this route, and 0028 s6 is the closer precedent: rate limiting is a PRECONDITION of mounting an unauthenticated route, enforced as the first plug, keyed on conn.remote_ip. 0042 must say the new mount follows 0028 s6, reuses Letflow.Plugs.PublicReadRateLimit.Bucket (lib/letflow/plugs/ public_read_rate_limit/bucket.ex) or a mount-point-agnostic successor, and does not discharge 0040's deferred authenticated limiter.
Also to be read and respected, confirmed not in conflict unless the design finds otherwise: 0002 (OIDC library/verification -- the token path is unchanged), 0022 (BilimBaga vertical: its users are the motivating case; no per-vertical code), 0038 point 4 (realm-resolution chain unchanged), 0012 (mobile stack), 0016 (secrets by reference).
THE DESIGN DOCUMENT (lib/letflow/design/req434-email-first-login- directory.md) MUST SPECIFY, with source citations, not assertions:
(a) Directory schema. A public-schema (global) table, e.g. tenant_login_directory, alongside tenants and tenant_memberships, outside every tenant schema (INV-1 storage unchanged). Columns limited to an email key, tenant_id (real FK to tenants, ON DELETE CASCADE) and timestamps; unique (email key, tenant_id). It is a pointer table: no password, role, session or profile fields. Distinguish it from tenant_memberships (REQ-384): memberships are admin-linked cross-tenant switch targets; the directory is a login-routing index of where an account exists. Decide whether one table or a unification is right and say why; recommended: separate tables, one shared normalisation function (Letflow.Identity.TenantMembership.normalize_subject_key/1 -- one implementation on both sides, per its own moduledoc).
(b) Email key form. Recommended default: a keyed HMAC-SHA256 of the normalised email (lower-case, trim) with the pepper supplied by secret REFERENCE (INV-4, decision 0016), not plaintext, because the lookup only ever needs equality on an email the caller just typed, and delivery (REQ-437) uses that typed address, never a stored one. State the trade-off against tenant_memberships' plaintext subject_key. Flagged as an open question below.
(c) Population signals. Letflow has no Keycloak Admin client in lib/ (REQ-135/137 are survey/design only; realm and user creation happen in Keycloak outside Letflow). The in-Letflow signals are therefore Letflow.Identity.create_user/2 (lib/letflow/identity.ex:227, reached from POST /api/v1/users, authz_post '/users', :UsersManage in lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex) and Letflow.Identity.provision_oidc_user/4 (identity.ex:127, JIT on first login). Specify whether the directory write is in the same Ecto.Multi/transaction as the user insert (recommended, matching create_user's existing Audit.append_multi shape), the removal semantics on user deletion or deactivation (POST /users/:id/status), email change, and tenant deactivation (tenants.status :inactive). Keycloak-side-only accounts (created in the realm admin console but never seen by Letflow) are NOT in the directory until their first login or a backfill; say so as a documented limitation. VERIFIED GAPS the design must resolve, not assume: (1) tenant_id source -- create_user/2 (identity.ex:227), update_user_profile/3 (:337) and update_user_status/3 (:389) receive only opts[:prefix], never a tenant_id. Recommended: a new required :tenant_id key in their opts, supplied by their callers in lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex from conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id (never a request parameter); rejected alternative: a reverse prefix->tenant lookup (extra query, a second source of tenant identity). provision_oidc_user/4 already has tenant_id. (2) users.email has no unique index (only username and (external_realm, external_id) are unique), so two active users in one tenant may share an email; the removal rule is: delete a directory entry only if no OTHER ACTIVE user in that tenant has the same normalised email. (3) Identity has no delete_user function, so 'user deletion' has no code path; erasure is tenant deletion (FK cascade), tenant deactivation (status filtered at query time) and the status/email-change paths. (4) The status hook lives INSIDE Identity.update_user_status/3 (same transaction), not in the router handler; likewise the profile hook inside update_user_profile/3.
(d) Backfill. An idempotent mix task (naming per lib/mix/tasks/ letflow.backfill_*.ex precedent) iterating tenants and reading each tenant schema's users.email through the existing per-tenant :prefix derivation (TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1). Open question on the source (below).
(e) The lookup endpoint contract: method (recommended POST with the email in the JSON body, never a query string, so it is not written to access logs), request/response shape, the closed response allowlist (hand-built map, literal keys, per 0028), and the single-round-trip rule (one directory query joined to tenants for status and display name; no second lookup on the miss path; a malformed email must not short-circuit ahead of that query). Return a realm SLUG and display name only -- never idp_realm_id, tenant UUID, or an authority URL (INV-2, INV-9: the SPA derives the authority via the existing GET /api/tenant-config?realm=).
(f) Anti-enumeration, honestly bounded. Unknown email and known email must be indistinguishable in status, body shape and bounded timing. A single-match redirect inherently tells the caller 'this email has an account in tenant X'; the design must state this as the accepted bounded inference (or choose the strict mode as the default), and list the mitigations (limiter, per-email throttle, no bulk route, uniform response in the strict mode below). State plainly that the considered-and-rejected trick 'always redirect unknown emails to bpm-default' leaks any non-default tenant's membership by contrast, and why it is or is not used.
(g) Disclosure modes (application config, not code). Mode A, 'uniform_plus_email': the endpoint always returns the same neutral response (HTTP 202, identical body, delivery work done off the request path so timing does not depend on a match); the tenant list, whether one tenant or many, reaches the user only by email. Mode B, 'redirect_single': exactly one match returns the realm slug directly (UX-optimal; carries the bounded inference of (f)); several matches or none return the same neutral response and the list is emailed. The ORIGINAL user requirement, recorded as written: 'respond uniformly and deliver the tenant list by email unless the email matches exactly one tenant' -- that is Mode B, the user's stated shape. The design must reconcile Mode B with the anti-enumeration goal and record the chosen default (see open_questions); it must NOT silently pick.
(h) Keycloak interplay. login_hint: the SPA passes the typed email to signinRedirect so the realm login page pre-fills the username (oidc-client-ts signin args; interacts with buildRedirectArgs in web/src/auth/oidcRedirectArgs.ts and the redirect_uri ?realm= embedding from ISS-0726). kc_idp_hint selects a brokered identity provider inside a realm and is NOT applicable (no realm brokers an IdP today); state that it is deliberately unused. login_hint populates the username field only; realms whose users log in by username need 'Login with email' enabled for a typed email to work -- list that as a realm-configuration precondition and state who checks it (UAT).
(i) Security invariants touched, by number: INV-1 (directory outside tenant schemas; backfill reads each tenant schema only via the derived prefix), INV-2 (closed response allowlist), INV-4 (pepper by reference; no raw email in logs or telemetry), INV-5 (known/unknown email indistinguishability -- INV-5's text is about resource ids; this is its first email-keyed instance), INV-6 (new data-access path must prove scoping), INV-7 (no SQL interpolation in backfill), INV-8 (notifier, mail or DB failure on the public path must return the same neutral response, not a 500, not a crash), INV-9 (no tenant-controlled outbound URL: the server never builds a redirect from tenant-supplied text). INV-3 does not apply. SECURITY-REVIEWER is a mandatory gate on 0042 AND on REQ-435/436/437 implementation.
(j) Mobile tier NOTE (not a spec). The mobile bootstrap resolves the tenant from a deep-link subdomain or manual slug entry (docs/mobile/ requirements.md MOB-2, REQ-421, REQ-124's /api/mobile/tenant-config) and is unaffected. The new endpoint is additive and unauthenticated, so a later mobile requirement may adopt it in place of manual slug entry; the design records that as a future option and that neither the endpoint nor the response may assume a browser. docs/mobile/ is not edited here.
(k) Future, explicitly out of scope: SSO across realms or a single identity spanning tenants (0006 D1/0038 keep one account per realm); a platform-level Keycloak broker realm.
(l) Fallback precedence in the SPA, as a table: (1) sessionStorage bpm_realm_slug, (2) ?realm= query parameter, (3) the email-first screen, (4) host lookup (GET /api/tenant-config?host=) and its bpm-default fallback retained for single-tenant/dev deployments. DECIDED HERE as the recommended precedence (to be ratified): host binding does not exist today (tenant_config by host has no host->tenant binding by design, REQ-076), so host lookup never identifies a tenant and is NOT ranked above the email-first screen. Order: explicit ?realm= > stored slug > email-first screen when the flag is on > default-realm fallback (host lookup, then bpm-default). Note today's resolveRealmFromUrl() reads the stored slug BEFORE ?realm=; the design must say how an explicit ?realm= overrides a stale stored value. A deployment with only the default tenant uses the flag (see open_questions). REQ-438 implements exactly this order.
requirement_text.REQ-435:
Implements the data layer of the directory as specified by REQ-434's design and decision 0042 (lib/letflow/design/req434-email-first-login- directory.md); where this text and that design differ, the design governs and the difference is flagged to REQ-VALIDATOR, not silently resolved. SPLIT (BA decision D-F, decision 0043): this entry builds the migration, the schema module, the pepper and key-id handling, the read/upsert functions and the backfill. The population hooks inside the Identity transactions, the JIT transaction, the explicit :tenant_id opt with its guard and the removal rule are REQ-440. The limiter is REQ-436, the lookup endpoint REQ-437, the SPA REQ-438.
WRINKLE (state, do not paper over): decision 0028's 'a table lands with its first writer' rule, restated as 0042 Standing prohibition 13, is satisfied only by REQ-435 and REQ-440 landing back to back. Until REQ-440 is done the backfill is the only writer, so the table is populated once and goes stale. REQ-437 must not be claimed for done before REQ-440 is done (REQ-437 depends_on lists it). The letter of 0042 prohibition 13 ('REQ-435 ships the table together with every writer') is amended by decision 0043 D-F; flagged for REVIEWER.
BUILDS: 1. A migration under priv/repo/migrations/ creating the public-schema directory table tenant_login_directory (global, alongside tenants/ tenant_memberships; never created per tenant schema), per design s1.1: email_key bytea (32 bytes, CHECK), tenant_id FK ON DELETE CASCADE, composite primary key (email_key, tenant_id) which is the unique (key, tenant_id) index, a (tenant_id) index, inserted_at, PLUS a new NOT NULL key_id column (short identifier of the pepper that produced email_key, BA decision D-C; amends design s1.1). key_id is NOT part of the primary key: the key bytes already differ per pepper, so the pair (email_key, tenant_id) stays the identity. Reversible. 2. A schema module Letflow.Identity.TenantLoginDirectoryEntry (lib/letflow/identity/, moduledoc in the style of tenant_membership.ex with an explicit 'what this table is not' paragraph) and a new context Letflow.LoginDirectory with: email_key/1, sentinel_key/0, the lookup (lookup_by_key/1 and lookup_by_email/1 of design s5.4, amended by item 4 below), upsert_entry/2 (writes under the CURRENT key id only) and the shared normalisation (reuse TenantMembership.normalize_subject_key/1 and the extracted public email_shape?/1 of design s1.5; do not fork either). The removal function remove_entry_if_unreferenced/3 and the plan functions belong to REQ-440. 3. PEPPER PROVISIONING AND KEY ID (BA decision D-C; supersedes design s2.4 'dual-pepper window not built', design Q8 and 0042 OQ-6): a. Per-environment HMAC pepper of at least 32 random bytes, supplied by the environment's secrets store through the environment variable LETFLOW_LOGIN_DIRECTORY_PEPPER (64 hex characters = 32 random bytes, design s2.2) and NEVER committed to the repository, a fixture, a Dockerfile, a compose file or a handoff. Dev supplies it through an ordinary environment variable (documented in .env.example with no working value, as .env.example:11 does for the master key); config/ test.exs injects a fixed non-trivial test value and key id. b. A key id: LETFLOW_LOGIN_DIRECTORY_PEPPER_ID (required alongside the pepper; lowercase letters, digits, '-' and '_', 1..32 characters, for example 'p2026a'). Every directory row records the key id of the pepper that produced its email_key. c. DUAL-READ DURING ROTATION: an optional previous pepper, LETFLOW_LOGIN_DIRECTORY_PEPPER_PREVIOUS with LETFLOW_LOGIN_DIRECTORY_PEPPER_PREVIOUS_ID (both or neither; absent in steady state). While present, the lookup computes the candidate key set {current key, previous key} and finds rows under either; writes and the backfill use the current key and key id only. config/runtime.exs validates at boot, with the same checks as the master key (config/runtime.exs:30-72): absent -> raise; not 64 hex -> raise; all-zero or all-0xFF -> raise; equal to the secrets master key -> raise; previous equal to current, previous id equal to current id, or only one of the previous pair set -> raise. No message echoes a value. d. ROTATION TOOLING IS NOT HERE: the retire_key and key_status mix tasks and the rotation runbook docs/runbooks/login-directory-pepper- rotation.md are REQ-443 (split out so this entry stays one agent turn; depends_on this entry). Serving lookups needs only a, b, c above; a deployed pepper needs a rotation procedure, which is why REQ-444's enablement gate requires REQ-443 done before the feature is enabled outside dev. 4. DESIGN INTERPLAY FLAGGED, NOT SILENTLY RESOLVED (see open_questions and decision 0043 'Conflicts flagged for REVIEWER'): the key id touches design s5.3 (sentinel_key/0), s5.4 (lookup_by_key/1 takes one key), s12.2 (consume_email(email_key, kind)) and s3.7 (advisory lock derived from (tenant_id, email_key)). PROPOSED resolution, to be confirmed by CODE-DESIGNER/REVIEWER before the build starts, and the acceptance criteria below are written to it: (i) the lookup takes a key LIST and issues ONE query (email_key = ANY(keys)) selecting DISTINCT tenants, so the match count is a count of distinct tenants and the Mode B 'exactly one match' rule is unaffected by a person holding a row under each key; (ii) sentinel_key/0 likewise yields one sentinel per candidate key, so the query shape and the number of HMACs are the same for every input (constant per deployment state, never per input); (iii) the per-email limiter buckets (REQ-436) key on the CURRENT key only, so a rotation resets per-address buckets once and nothing else; (iv) writers take the advisory lock on the current key and the removal (REQ-440) deletes under every candidate key. 5. An idempotent mix task (lib/mix/tasks/letflow.backfill_login_ directory.ex, following letflow.backfill_platform_roles.ex / letflow.backfill_task_assignee_type.ex) that iterates ALL REGISTERED tenants via TenantProvisioning.list_registrations/0 regardless of tenant status (design s0.3 D3: tenant status is filtered at query time), reads each tenant schema's users.email (active users only) via the TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1 prefix (no string- interpolated schema in SQL, INV-7), writes entries under the current key and key id with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, supports --dry-run, prints per-tenant counts, never logs an email, treats a failure in one tenant as reported-and-skipped (INV-8), and is the re-keying step of a rotation (rerun after the pepper changes). KNOWN LIMITATION (BA decision D-E; NOTE only, no requirement): the backfill source is the tenant users table. A Keycloak-only account that has never logged in to Letflow and is not in a tenant users table is invisible to the directory until its first login (it falls back to ?realm=/stored slug/default). An optional future Keycloak-sync requirement could close it; it is not scoped here.
requirement_text.REQ-436:
The mounting precondition for REQ-437's unauthenticated mount, per decision 0028 s6 and REQ-434 / 0042. Split out of the endpoint entry so each is one agent turn. SECURITY-REVIEWER is a hard gate (INV-5, INV-8: a limiter that shares state with another mount, or grows without bound, is a defect on a multi-tenant platform). Where this text and the merged design (lib/letflow/design/req434-email-first-login-directory.md, s12) differ, the design governs; the amendments below are the design's s0.3 corrections D5, D6, D10, D11, D13 and D14 and REQ-VALIDATOR must accept them.
VERIFIED STARTING POINT: Letflow.Plugs.PublicReadRateLimit.Bucket (lib/letflow/plugs/public_read_rate_limit/bucket.ex) exposes consume(key, capacity, refill_per_sec) over ONE named ETS table (:letflow_public_read_rate_limit) with bucket_key typed :global | {:ip, ip_address}, a check-then-write over :ets.lookup/:ets.insert (not :ets.update_counter/4), and NO eviction. Reusing it as-is would (a) share the :global bucket with /api/public, so flooding one mount would 429 the other, and (b) let an attacker grow the table without bound by submitting many distinct emails.
BUILDS: 1. A NEW sibling module, Letflow.Plugs.LoginDiscoveryRateLimit.Bucket (lib/letflow/plugs/login_discovery_rate_limit/bucket.ex), a GenServer owning its own named ETS table (:letflow_login_discovery_rate_limit); every key it writes begins with :login_discovery. The existing Bucket and PublicReadRateLimit are NOT modified (git diff empty, their tests pass unmodified). This is the 'mount-point-agnostic successor' reading of REQ-434 item 4, not a refactor of the existing Bucket (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D10). Shared with the existing limiter: the token-bucket algorithm (restated with a cross-reference comment), the Response.rate_limited + halt convention, 0028 s6 placement. 2. A plug Letflow.Plugs.LoginDiscoveryRateLimit (lib/letflow/plugs/), designed to run immediately after Letflow.Plugs.ClientIp (REQ-439) at the head of REQ-437's router chain, ahead of :match. The client address is conn.assigns.client_ip, falling back to conn.remote_ip when that assign is absent, and never a raw forwarded header (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D11: standing prohibition 8 is amended from 'keyed on conn.remote_ip' to the resolved client IP). The address is mapped to a bucket id with IPv6 aggregated to its /64 and an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address mapped to its IPv4 form (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D13). Order (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D13): the per-IP bucket is consumed FIRST; a refusal halts and does NOT touch the global bucket; only an IP-admitted request consumes the tighter global bucket. Both are checked before the body is read, so the 429 is input-independent for them. The per-email buckets are exposed as consume_email(email_key, kind :: :request | :send) for the endpoint to call after it computes the email key (the body is not parseable by a pre-:match plug without breaking the first-plug rule). Every refusal (IP, global, per-email) goes through ONE send_rate_limited/1 constructor, so the 429 status, headers (including a constant Retry-After) and body are identical by construction with no email-dependent content. 3. Bounded state (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D5, D13). Only LOSSLESS eviction: a periodic sweep deletes exactly the rows whose tokens have refilled to capacity (behaviourally identical to an absent row); a live (non-idle) key is never evicted, so a victim bucket cannot be refilled faster than its normal rate. Two key populations, two caps: email-kind keys (:email_hmac and :email_send) bounded by max_email_keys with a boot-time validate_config!/1 invariant (max_email_keys >= 2 * (global_capacity + ceil(global_refill_per_sec * (T_email_full_max + sweep_interval_s)))), and IP keys bounded by a hard max_ip_keys cap. At a cap, an inline sweep runs and, if still full, the NEW key is refused fail closed (an IP-key refusal does not consume a global token). consume is a compare-and-swap with bounded retries, failing closed on exhaustion, and inserts new keys with an insert-if-absent primitive. Capacities, refill rates, caps, sweep interval and retry-after come from application config (config :letflow, Letflow.Plugs.LoginDiscoveryRateLimit, ...) with the defaults of design s12.4, not hardcoded. 4. A fourth bucket kind, {:login_discovery, :email_send, h} (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D6): the per-address minimum send interval (default 1 token, refill 1/900 s, i.e. one notifier send per address per 15 minutes), consumed through consume_email(key, :send) by REQ-437's notifier task. Added to this entry rather than REQ-437 (design Q5). 5. Non-identifying outcome counters (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D14): one telemetry event [:letflow, :login_discovery, :outcome], measurement %{count: 1}, single metadata key outcome, emitted by this limiter with exactly :rate_limited_ip, :rate_limited_global or :rate_limited_email; metadata carries no email, key, IP, slug or tenant id. 6. It does NOT discharge the deferred authenticated Letflow.Plugs.RateLimit row in lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex (decision 0040) and does not modify AuthPipeline.
requirement_text.REQ-437:
Implements the lookup mount specified by REQ-434's design and decision 0042, on top of REQ-435's directory, REQ-436's limiter and REQ-439's client-IP resolution. SECURITY-REVIEWER is a named hard gate on this entry (new unauthenticated, caller-keyed data path: INV-1, INV-2, INV-4, INV-5, INV-6, INV-8, INV-9). Where this text and the ratified design differ, the design governs; the amendments below are the design's s0.3 corrections D7, D8, D11, D12 and D14 and REQ-VALIDATOR must accept them.
The response contract is PARAMETRISED BY AN EXPLICIT CONFIG MODE (config :letflow, Letflow.Routers.LoginDiscovery, mode: :uniform_plus_email | :redirect_single, env LETFLOW_LOGIN_DISCOVERY_MODE). The two modes have different equivalence classes and every test below names its mode. The default is Mode B (:redirect_single), RATIFIED as the default disclosure mode by REVIEWER and SECURITY-REVIEWER (design Q1); Mode A is switchable by config. - mode :uniform_plus_email: every request, whatever it matches, gets the same neutral response; known and unknown addresses are byte-identical. - mode :redirect_single: exactly one active-tenant match returns the realm slug and display name; several matches and no matches both get the same neutral response, byte-identical to each other (the tenant list for several matches goes by email through the notifier). A single match is DISCLOSED by design (the bounded inference of REQ-434 (f)); it is not claimed indistinguishable from unknown.
PER-TENANT DISCLOSURE (BA decision D-A, decision 0043; the per-tenant setting, its migration and its write path are REQ-442, a depends_on of this entry): the deployment-wide mode above stays the default and is the fallback and ceiling; each tenant may be set to uniform. The lookup happens by email before the tenant is known, so the effective mode is a rule over the MATCH SET: return the single-match 200 ONLY if there is exactly one active match AND that match's disclose flag (from REQ-442's lookup) is true; in every other case return the neutral response, and still email the list as before (a single match in a uniform tenant is delivered [t], like Mode A). A uniform-tenant address is therefore byte-identical to an unknown one. Rate limiting stays on in all modes. Uniform is RECOMMENDED for candidate-facing tenants (for example Bilimbaga exam candidates).
ENABLEMENT GATE (BA decision D-D, decision 0043): the feature stays OFF outside dev until a named person confirms the lawful basis and controller (0042 OQ-3). That gate is made testable by REQ-444 (split out of this entry), not left to procedure; this entry only fixes the notifier adapter key the gate reads (BUILDS item 9).
BUILDS: 1. Letflow.Routers.LoginDiscovery (lib/letflow/routers/), mounted in lib/letflow/router.ex as a sibling forward (path per the design, recommended '/api/login-discovery') declared BEFORE forward('/api/v1', Letflow.Plugs.ApiPipeline), like /api/tenant-config at router.ex:111. It is NOT mounted under /api/public (decision 0028) and AuthPipeline is not modified. One route: POST with the email in the JSON body. A catch-all and wrong methods return the platform's standard 404 (Letflow.Api.Response.not_found/1). The chain starts with Letflow.Plugs.ClientIp (REQ-439) then REQ-436's limiter plug, ahead of :match (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D11); the endpoint additionally calls REQ-436's per-email check. Any per-IP keying is on the resolved client IP (conn.assigns.client_ip), not conn.remote_ip (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D11, standing prohibition 8 amended). 2. MOUNT SWITCH (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D12): config :letflow, Letflow.Routers.LoginDiscovery, enabled: boolean() (default false in :prod, true in dev/test; the env LETFLOW_LOGIN_DISCOVERY_ENABLED and the :prod boot refusal are owned by REQ-439). The router's enabled_gate/2 returns the route-level standard 404 for EVERY method and path when disabled, before ClientIp and the limiter run, issuing zero queries and creating no limiter state. 3. Resolution via the directory's lookup_by_email/1 from REQ-435: ONE database round trip before any response decision, for matched, unmatched and malformed input alike (a malformed email is normalised to a fixed sentinel so the query count does not differ; there is no early-return branch ahead of the query), and no second query to improve an error message. 4. A hand-built success body with literal keys; the only tenant fields ever present are slug and display name; never idp_realm_id, tenant UUID, authority URL, user id or counts of other accounts. 'slug' here means tenants.slug, the value ?realm= and /api/tenant-config accept, not idp_realm_id (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D8, a note on REQ-434's wording; REQ-434 itself is not edited). 5. A notifier PORT: a behaviour (e.g. Letflow.LoginDiscovery.Notifier, @callback deliver_tenant_list/2) invoked off the request path (Task.Supervisor child, so request timing does not depend on a match or on mail latency), a default adapter that DELIVERS NOTHING and logs only a non-identifying counter (no email, no tenant), and a test double. The task consumes REQ-436's :send bucket (consume_email(key, :send)) before delivering (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D6). The real SMTP/mail adapter is explicitly NOT built here (Letflow has no mailer); until one exists, paths that depend on email delivery degrade safely to the neutral response. Notifier failure or crash must not alter the HTTP response (INV-8). 6. Non-identifying outcome counters (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D14): exactly one [:letflow, :login_discovery, :outcome] event per request (measurement %{count: 1}, single metadata key outcome). This endpoint emits :tenant (the Mode B single-match 200), :accepted (every 202, whatever the cause, so the event does not split known/multi/unknown/malformed) and :not_found (wrong method or path on an enabled mount); enabled_gate/2 ALWAYS emits :disabled. REQ-436 emits the three :rate_limited_* outcomes. No email, key, IP, slug, tenant id or count in the metadata. 7. OpenAPI/spec coverage: no-op. No OpenAPI artefact exists in the repository (decision 0010), so there is nothing to change; the handoff records that fact (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D7). 8. EFFECTIVE-MODE DECISION (D-A): Letflow.LoginDiscovery.decide/2 and delivery/2 (design s7) take the lookup's per-match disclose flag (REQ-442) instead of re-deriving a mode per tenant: decision is {:match, t} iff exactly one active match and its disclose is true, else :neutral; delivery is {:deliver, list} for two or more matches, {:deliver, [t]} for one non-disclosed match, :none for none or failure and for a disclosed single match. disclose is stripped before any body is built; the response allowlist, status codes, one-query and one-submission rules are unchanged. The deployment mode remains LETFLOW_LOGIN_DISCOVERY_MODE (default :redirect_single). 9. NOTIFIER ADAPTER KEY (named explicitly so REQ-441 and REQ-444 use the same one): the adapter is selected by the application-env key `config :letflow, Letflow.LoginDiscovery.Notifier, adapter: <module>` (design s13), default Letflow.LoginDiscovery.Notifier.Noop in config/config.exs, the test double in config/test.exs. The enablement gate (defaults, boot refusal, confirmation marker) is NOT built here: it is REQ-444 (split out so this entry stays one agent turn).
requirement_text.REQ-438:
The web/ half of the feature, per REQ-434's design and decision 0042. Credentials are NEVER entered in the SPA (decision 0035's core decision stands): the new page collects an email address only, then hands off to Keycloak's hosted login unchanged. Mode B (:redirect_single) is the RATIFIED default disclosure mode (REVIEWER and SECURITY-REVIEWER; Mode A is switchable by backend config), and the closed response union below is the same under both modes.
CURRENT BEHAVIOUR TO CHANGE (verified in the tree): web/src/auth/ ProtectedRoute.tsx on !isAuthenticated immediately calls getOidcManager().then(m => m.signinRedirect(buildRedirectArgs(...))); the realm comes from resolveRealmFromUrl() in web/src/auth/tenantConfig.ts (sessionStorage 'bpm_realm_slug', then ?realm=, else null -> GET /api/tenant-config?host= -> bpm-default fallback). A user in another tenant with no ?realm= is sent to the wrong realm (ISS-0727).
PRECEDENCE (decided in REQ-434 (l); host binding does not exist today -- tenant_config by host has no host->tenant binding by design, REQ-076 -- so a host lookup never identifies a tenant and is not ranked above the email-first screen): (1) an explicit ?realm= query parameter, (2) a stored 'bpm_realm_slug' from a previous load, (3) the email-first screen when the email-first flag is on, (4) otherwise the default-realm fallback exactly as today (host lookup then bpm-default). Note: today's resolveRealmFromUrl() reads the stored slug BEFORE ?realm=; the implementation must make an explicit ?realm= win and update the stored value, and must not change behaviour when only one of the two is present.
BUILDS: 1. A public route (e.g. '/login', registered in web/src/router.tsx OUTSIDE ProtectedRoute) and page component under web/src/pages/ with an email field, client-side shape validation only, submit, and the states the platform already demands of data screens (loading, error, neutral). User-facing strings go through the existing i18n mechanism (decision 0021, web/src/i18n/). The page also carries a static ORGANISATION-CODE control (a text input for the tenant slug, not a credential) present in EVERY state (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D14; design s11.5): its submit navigates to /?realm=<url-encoded code> with no discovery call; validation is non-empty and length <= 255 only. The 429, network-failure and malformed-response states therefore offer the ?realm= route, so a 429 is never a dead end (design s12.8). 2. A typed API client function (web/src/api/loginDiscovery.ts, beside memberships.ts) for the REQ-437 route, using the existing web/src/api/client.ts, with the response type as a closed union matching the design's matrix. 3. Outcomes: slug returned -> store it exactly as resolveRealmFromUrl() does (sessionStorage 'bpm_realm_slug') so buildRedirectArgs embeds ?realm= in redirect_uri (ISS-0726 behaviour preserved), then call signinRedirect with login_hint = the typed email, via the existing OidcManager / tenantOidcRegistry path (fetching that realm's config with the existing GET /api/tenant-config?realm=); neutral response -> a single fixed message that never says whether the address exists (and, where the mode emails a list, says only that instructions were sent if the address is registered); no tenant picker is built: neither disclosure mode returns tenant names for the multi-match case (design s11.5). 4. ProtectedRoute wiring per the PRECEDENCE above, preserving the pre-redirect path via the existing isSafeRestorePath/state mechanism (web/src/auth/safeRestorePath.ts). The email-first flag (build/config, per REQ-434's answer) disables the screen for single-tenant and dev/E2E deployments, restoring today's behaviour exactly. 5. AuthProvider paths (design req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D4; the earlier text wrongly said both paths clear the stored realm; only logout() does, AuthProvider.tsx ~131-141, while session-expired at ~85-95 retains it and re-logs into the same realm). Logout is unchanged: it clears the stored realm (__tests__/AuthProvider.logout-clears-realm.test.tsx behaviour kept) and, with the flag on, the next unauthenticated load lands on the email-first page via ProtectedRoute. Session-expired is unchanged when a realm is stored; when none is stored and the flag is on, it navigates to /login instead of calling signinRedirect against the default realm. 6. Tests: Vitest unit/component tests, a new i18n-grep test in the style of web/src/__tests__/entities-i18n-grep.test.ts covering the new page (no general hardcoded-string guard exists in web/tests/guards today -- decision 0021 is enforced per area by such grep tests), and a Playwright (or the existing e2e harness) path for the real flow; add a UAT scenario fixture only if it satisfies mix letflow.check_uat_scenario_schema, otherwise record the gap.
requirement_text.REQ-439:
Working label REQ-CIP. Added by design lib/letflow/design/req434-email-first-login-directory.md s0.3 D11 and s15.0 (spec: s12.6) and 0042 (OQ-5, resolved by design): in the real topology (Cloudflare -> nginx -> published container port -> Bandit) conn.remote_ip is the proxy hop, the same for every visitor, so a per-IP bucket keyed on it would be ONE shared bucket and one visitor could 429 everyone. This entry makes the per-IP key the real client address. It is a depends_on of REQ-436 and REQ-437 and a precondition for enabling the login-discovery feature. SECURITY-REVIEWER is a hard gate (INV-4, INV-5: a spoofable limiter key). Mode B (:redirect_single) is the ratified default disclosure mode (REVIEWER and SECURITY-REVIEWER), which is why the per-IP bound must be real; the mode itself is not touched here.
BUILDS: 1. lib/letflow/plugs/client_ip.ex: Letflow.Plugs.ClientIp, a mount-agnostic plug with the pure functions resolve(peer, x_real_ip_values, trusted_cidrs) :: :inet.ip_address(), parse_cidrs(String.t()) :: {:ok, [cidr]} | {:error, :invalid_cidr} and trusted?(ip, [cidr]) :: boolean(), cidr = {:inet.ip_address(), prefix_len 0..128}. No new dependency (CIDR matching is a small pure function over :inet). Rules, all failing safe toward the stricter shared bucket: (a) conn.assigns.client_ip is ALWAYS set and defaults to conn.remote_ip (empty trust list, or a peer outside the list: every forwarded header ignored, today's behaviour exactly); (b) only when the TCP peer conn.remote_ip is inside a trusted CIDR is X-Real-IP honoured, and only when there is exactly one header value that parses as a single IPv4 or IPv6 address (zero, several, a comma list or an unparsable value -> conn.remote_ip); (c) X-Forwarded-For is NEVER read; (d) conn.remote_ip itself is NOT rewritten, so PublicReadRateLimit and /api/public keep their current behaviour (their own limitation is 0042 OQ-12, noted not fixed). The plug reads no request body. 2. Configuration: env LETFLOW_TRUSTED_PROXIES (comma-separated CIDRs, read once at boot into config :letflow, Letflow.Plugs.ClientIp, trusted_proxies: [cidr]; an invalid entry raises at boot; unset = []), env LETFLOW_LOGIN_DISCOVERY_ENABLED (true/false, any other value raises) feeding the mount switch config :letflow, Letflow.Routers.LoginDiscovery, enabled: boolean() (default false when config_env() == :prod, true in dev/test), in config/runtime.exs and config/config.exs, with a test default of [] in config/test.exs and the names (no real values) documented in deploy/.env.example. The router gate that READS enabled is REQ-437's. 3. :prod BOOT REFUSAL: config/runtime.exs raises at boot when config_env() == :prod, LETFLOW_LOGIN_DISCOVERY_ENABLED is true and LETFLOW_TRUSTED_PROXIES is empty or unset (message names both variables, contains no value). Outside :prod the same combination logs one fixed warning at boot. 4. deploy/nginx/letflow-test.conf: add the realip directives (set_real_ip_from for the Cloudflare edge ranges and real_ip_header CF-Connecting-IP, ngx_http_realip_module) so $remote_addr is the visitor before the existing proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr. Whether Cloudflare sends CF-Connecting-IP and its ranges are external knowledge (design U3) the implementer must verify. QA's vhost is outside this repository (design U4): the exact directives are recorded in the handoff as an infrastructure action.
FILES. Create: lib/letflow/plugs/client_ip.ex, test/letflow/plugs/client_ip_test.exs, test/letflow/client_ip_runtime_config_test.exs (env parsing, modelled on secrets_runtime_config_test.exs). Change: config/runtime.exs, config/config.exs, config/test.exs, deploy/.env.example, deploy/nginx/letflow-test.conf. NOT changed (git diff empty): lib/letflow/plugs/public_read_rate_limit.ex and its bucket.ex, lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex, lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex.
requirement_text.REQ-440:
The writers of the directory REQ-435 builds, exactly as specified by REQ-434's design (lib/letflow/design/req434-email-first-login- directory.md s3) and decision 0042. Where this text and the design differ, the design governs and the difference is flagged to REQ-VALIDATOR. This text is the 'b' half of the former REQ-435 and its BUILDS items are carried over unchanged in substance; they are not new scope.
WRINKLE (state, do not paper over): decision 0028's 'a table lands with its first writer' rule (0042 Standing prohibition 13) is satisfied only by REQ-435 and this entry landing back to back. Between them the backfill alone populates the table. REQ-437 depends_on this entry and MUST NOT be claimed for done before it.
PR #2201 (queue Q-944, worker letflow-4-worker-q944, branch feat/REQ-435-login-directory, merge held) currently implements ALL of the former REQ-435, including these hooks, in one branch. If the whole of it lands as one change, this entry's BUILDS are satisfied by that change and are closed by RELEASE-VALIDATOR verification (re-deriving every acceptance criterion below against the merged code) instead of being re-implemented. The PR is not touched by this entry.
BUILDS: 1. Population hooks INSIDE the Identity context functions, in the SAME Ecto.Multi/transaction as the source write -- not in router handlers: Letflow.Identity.create_user/2 (lib/letflow/identity.ex:227, its existing Multi with Audit.append_multi), update_user_status/3 (identity.ex:389) and update_user_profile/3 (identity.ex:337, when the email changes). A user with a nil email writes no row. The pure plan function plan_user_change/2 and apply_plan/3 of design s3.3 are the single source of truth for add/remove. No route is added and no existing response shape changes. 2. JIT TRANSACTION (design s0.3 D2): the JIT insert in provision_oidc_user/4 (insert_or_fetch/4, identity.ex ~1766-1809, created: true path) is NOT inside any transaction today; wrap the JIT insert, its created-check and the directory upsert in a NEW Repo.transaction (only a genuinely created row writes an entry; a directory failure aborts the transaction and returns {:error, {:login_directory, reason}}); sync_role_claims_from_token/3 stays outside it. Savepoint-mode insert per design s3.5 so the username-race recovery still runs in a live transaction. 3. TENANT_ID SOURCE: create_user/2, update_user_profile/3 and update_user_status/3 receive only opts[:prefix] today. Add a new required :tenant_id opt supplied by their callers in lib/letflow/ routers/identity.ex from conn.assigns.auth_context.tenant_id (never a request parameter), :prefix semantics unchanged, every other caller updated or proven to need no directory write. Fail-closed guard before any write: schema_name_for_tenant(tenant_id) must equal opts[:prefix] ({:error, :invalid_tenant_id} for a malformed id, {:error, :tenant_prefix_mismatch} for a valid id naming a different schema, {:error, :tenant_id_required} when missing), writing nothing on any of them. Rationale as in design s0.3 D1 (a reverse prefix derivation is pure and costs no query; it is rejected because it can never detect a mismatch). 4. REMOVAL RULE (verified: users.email carries no unique index): remove_entry_if_unreferenced/3 deletes the entry only if no OTHER active user in that tenant schema has the same normalised email, under EVERY candidate key (current and, during a rotation, previous; BA decision D-C, REQ-435 item 4(iv)), serialised by the advisory lock of design s3.7. Identity has no delete_user function, so deletion has no path to hook; 0042 Standing prohibition 14 binds any future deletion path. 5. Test-only escape opt `login_directory: :skip` per design s3.2/s15.1, honoured only for tests.
requirement_text.REQ-441:
Implements the real mail adapter behind the notifier PORT that REQ-437 specifies (Letflow.LoginDiscovery.Notifier, @callback deliver_tenant_list/2, design s13) and replaces its non-delivering default for deployments that enable the feature. REQUIRED before the email-first feature flag can be enabled outside dev (REQ-444's boot refusal treats the non-delivering Noop adapter as not real, and REQ-444 depends_on this entry). Provider-agnostic: the port is the abstraction; SMTP is the first adapter. SECURITY-REVIEWER is a named hard gate (new external egress, INV-4 credentials, INV-8, INV-9, INV-5 uniformity).
FIRST STEP, before any implementation (WF-02): a CODE-DESIGNER pass that chooses the mail library, records the choice as a decision record under docs/migration/decisions/ and designs the adapter, its configuration and its failure handling. This entry adds a runtime dependency, so the library choice is a decision, not an implementation detail; ELIXIR-DEV does not start until that design has passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR.
NOTE ONLY, out of scope: the same adapter is expected to serve invitations and password recovery later. Nothing here builds those, and the port is not widened for them; a later requirement may add callbacks.
BUILDS: 1. An SMTP adapter module implementing the REQ-437 notifier behaviour (for example Letflow.LoginDiscovery.Notifier.Smtp), plus whatever mailer module the chosen library needs. Library choice (proposal: Swoosh with its SMTP adapter over gen_smtp; alternatives Bamboo or a bare gen_smtp) is made by CODE-DESIGNER and recorded as a decision record; mix.exs gains only that dependency. The hex dependency needs network for mix deps.get; if this environment cannot fetch it, say so explicitly rather than guessing. 2. Configuration by environment reference only (INV-4, no secret in the repository): LETFLOW_MAIL_ADAPTER (the adapter selector; unset or unknown keeps the Noop default, unknown value raises at boot), LETFLOW_SMTP_HOST, LETFLOW_SMTP_PORT, LETFLOW_SMTP_USERNAME, LETFLOW_SMTP_PASSWORD, LETFLOW_SMTP_TLS (verified TLS by default; plaintext only when explicitly set and never in :prod), LETFLOW_MAIL_FROM and the deployment base URL for any link (INV-9). Read once at boot in config/runtime.exs; with the adapter selected, a missing host, credentials or sender raises at boot with a message that echoes no value; .env.example (and deploy/.env.example) document the names with no working value. The password is never logged, never in a struct field that is inspected or serialised, and never in a crash report. 3. UNIFORM RESPONSE WHATEVER THE DELIVERY RESULT: delivery runs in the notifier task off the request path (REQ-437 item 5). A successful send, an SMTP rejection, a timeout, a connection or TLS failure and a raise all leave the HTTP status, headers and body byte-identical and add no per-request signal. Failure handling: no automatic retry in this requirement (a retry loop is an email-bombing amplifier; the per-address :send bucket of REQ-436 is consumed once per attempt, success or failure); the failure is recorded only as a non-identifying counter event [:letflow, :login_discovery, :notifier] with a single metadata key outcome in {:delivered, :failed, :skipped}, and a fixed log line carrying no address, tenant, slug, SMTP reply text or exception text. 4. A fixed message template (design s13 'message contract'): the only request-derived text is the recipient address; tenant slugs and display names appear as plain text; any link is built from the deployment base URL and the slug URL-encoded, never from tenant-controlled URL text; no HTML from tenant text (plain-text body, or HTML with all interpolated values escaped); subject and body fixed strings. 5. A capturing test adapter under test/support/ that records (recipient, tenants) calls and can be set to return {:error, _}, raise, exit or sleep. If REQ-437's test double already provides this, reuse it and add nothing; do not duplicate it. 6. ADAPTER SELECTION KEY: config/runtime.exs maps LETFLOW_MAIL_ADAPTER onto the application-env key `config :letflow, Letflow.LoginDiscovery.Notifier, adapter: <module>` (design s13; REQ-437 defines the key with the Noop default). A selected Smtp adapter with incomplete configuration refuses to boot (item 2). The enablement gate that treats Smtp as a real adapter is REQ-444, not built here.
requirement_text.REQ-442:
Decision D-A: Mode B (:redirect_single) stays the deployment-wide default; the disclosure mode becomes configurable per tenant with the deployment-wide mode as the fallback; 'uniform' (Mode A) is RECOMMENDED for candidate-facing tenants (for example Bilimbaga exam candidates). Rate limiting stays on in all modes. SIZING ANSWER: this does NOT fit REQ-437's sizing. It needs a schema change on tenants (public schema), a platform-admin write path with authorisation and response-shaping checks, and a change to the lookup query owned by REQ-435, none of which REQ-437 touches; REQ-437 is already one full turn. So it is its own requirement, and REQ-437 consumes its result.
The lookup happens by email BEFORE the tenant is known, so the effective-mode rule is defined over the MATCH SET (ORCH proposal, checked against design s10 and recorded in decision 0043): disclose slug and display name only if there is exactly ONE active match AND that tenant's effective mode is redirect_single; otherwise return the neutral response (and, as before, email the list). A uniform-tenant address is thereby indistinguishable from an unknown one. Checked against the ratified invariants: it does not break the Mode B equivalence class {multi, unknown, malformed, inactive-only, lookup-failure} (it only enlarges it with 'single match in a uniform tenant'), the single-query and no-early-return rules, the constant-work rule (the effective mode is computed in the same query; delivery stays one unconditional off-path submission) or the closed response allowlist; it DOES touch three ratified wordings, flagged below.
BUILDS: 1. A migration adding tenants.login_disclosure_mode (public schema, nullable string, CHECK in ('uniform_plus_email','redirect_single'); NULL = use the deployment-wide default). NOT stored in the tenant :settings blob: that blob has a closed key vocabulary whose values reach the pre-authentication /api/tenant-config and a tenant-admin write path (REQ-382), and the mode is a platform-security attribute that a tenant admin must not set or read. Reversible. 2. The Tenant schema field and a changeset path writable ONLY by PLATFORM_ADMIN through the existing platform-admin tenant update route (locate by grep which route calls Tenant.admin_patch_changeset/2 and extend that path; no new route unless none exists, in which case say so and stop for REQ-VALIDATOR). The change is audited as other platform-admin tenant updates are. A tenant admin's settings route rejects the key (closed vocabulary already does); GET /api/tenant-config and every tenant-admin-readable tenant shape do NOT contain it (INV-2); the platform-admin tenant response may. 3. LOOKUP EXTENSION in Letflow.LoginDirectory (REQ-435): the single query additionally yields, per matched tenant, a boolean disclose computed in SQL: the deployment mode is bound as a parameter; disclose = (deployment mode is redirect_single) AND COALESCE(tenants.login_disclosure_mode, 'redirect_single') = 'redirect_single'. The deployment-wide mode is thereby the fallback (tenant NULL) AND the ceiling (deployment :uniform_plus_email forces every tenant uniform, preserving 0042's configuration-only kill switch). The internal match type becomes %{slug, display_name, disclose}; disclose is consumed by REQ-437's decide/2 and is stripped before any response is built, so the response allowlist is unchanged. Still exactly one query, no tenant :prefix. 4. An unrecognised stored value cannot occur (CHECK); an unrecognised value read in code is treated as uniform.
requirement_text.REQ-443:
The operational half of BA decision D-C (per-environment pepper with a key id and dual-read rotation). REQ-435 builds the key id column, the pepper and key-id configuration with boot checks, the dual-read lookup and the re-keying backfill; this entry builds the tooling and the procedure an operator needs to rotate a deployed pepper. It is NOT a dependency of REQ-437 (serving lookups does not need rotation tooling); it IS a dependency of REQ-444 (a pepper that is deployed outside dev needs a rotation procedure before the feature is enabled there).
BUILDS: 1. A mix task letflow.login_directory.retire_key --key-id ID that deletes the directory rows carrying a retired key id. It refuses the current key id and a key id that is not present, supports --dry-run, and prints counts only. Every Repo call on the directory table carries log: false (design s3.9); no SQL is built by string interpolation (INV-7). 2. A mix task letflow.login_directory.key_status printing per-key-id row counts only. Neither task logs or prints an email, an email key or a pepper. 3. A rotation runbook at docs/runbooks/login-directory-pepper-rotation.md (a new directory: docs/ has no runbooks convention yet, flagged to REQ-VALIDATOR) covering: first provisioning per environment (generate 32 random bytes as 64 hex with a local tool, store in the environment's secrets store, never in the repository, chat or a handoff); the planned rotation (set the new pepper and id as current and the old as previous, deploy; run the backfill; verify with key_status that every previous-id row has a current-id counterpart; retire the previous id; remove the previous variables, deploy); the emergency rotation (suspected pepper exposure: immediate retire, accepting that discovery returns the neutral response and the SPA falls back to ?realm= until the backfill completes); rollback; and the EXTERNAL dependency on an ai-dala-infra secrets- inventory entry. The runbook contains no real value and no command that prints a secret.
requirement_text.REQ-444:
Makes the hard gate on enabling the feature outside dev (0042 OQ-3: a named person must confirm the lawful basis and controller) a TESTABLE configuration property instead of a procedure. The BA position on OQ-3 is PROPOSED only (decision 0043 D-D) and needs legal confirmation; this entry does not decide it, it enforces that nothing is enabled before someone has.
Dependency choice (keeps depends_on acyclic): the gate treats the notifier adapter as REAL only if it is on an explicit list of delivering adapters (initially Letflow.LoginDiscovery.Notifier.Smtp from REQ-441), and the test of that list uses the Smtp module, so this entry depends_on REQ-441. REQ-441 does not depend on this entry. The gate also requires the rotation procedure to exist (REQ-443), because a pepper deployed outside dev needs one.
BUILDS: 1. Shipped defaults: Letflow.Routers.LoginDiscovery enabled is false for :prod. config/config.exs sets enabled: config_env() != :prod (already in the tree, REQ-439); no config file (config/config.exs, config/prod.exs, runtime.exs defaults) sets it true for :prod; the server flag is never defaulted on by code. The SPA build flag VITE_EMAIL_FIRST_LOGIN (REQ-438) stays off by default in every non-dev build (REQ-438 carries that criterion). 2. A pure boot check (for example Letflow.LoginDiscovery.BootCheck.check/4 taking env, enabled?, confirmation marker and the value of the application-env key `config :letflow, Letflow.LoginDiscovery.Notifier, adapter:` that REQ-437 defines and REQ-441 sets via LETFLOW_MAIL_ADAPTER) called from config/runtime.exs after REQ-439's Letflow.Plugs.ClientIp.boot_check/3 (left unchanged). In any environment other than :dev and :test, when the mount is enabled, boot REFUSES (raises, echoing no value) unless ALL of: (i) the confirmation marker LETFLOW_LOGIN_DIRECTORY_LEGAL_CONFIRMATION is set to a non-blank value of at least 8 characters, which the operator sets only after a named person has confirmed OQ-3 (the value is that person's reference and a date; never logged); (ii) the configured notifier adapter is on the list of delivering adapters (not Noop, not the test double); (iii) the pepper and key id of REQ-435 are configured (its own boot checks already require them, asserted here as a precondition, not re-implemented). The marker cannot prove a confirmation happened; it makes enabling without one a deliberate, auditable act. 3. Rotation-procedure precondition: the rotation runbook of REQ-443 exists at docs/runbooks/login-directory-pepper-rotation.md (enforced as a repository test, since a runtime check of a document is not meaningful); the requirement ordering (depends_on REQ-443) is the real enforcement.

source_text.user_request: Coordinator task: produce a PROPOSED decision record (ADR) comparing identity options O1 (realm-per-tenant + platform directory + email-first login, REQ-434..444 as planned), O2 (GitHub/Google model: one central login realm, tenants as organisations/memberships), O3 (HYBRID: tenants declare auth mode 'shared' (users in central realm as org members) vs 'dedicated' (own realm and/or brokered company IdP/SAML), ONE entry point routing by email/domain/URL/invitation; the O1 directory is reused as the router). No implementation, no requirement edits (except the hold-note below).

context.adhoc_workflow: ADHOC-20261005-001: CODE-DESIGNER (ADR) -> CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR -> SECURITY-REVIEWER -> REVIEWER -> ORCH branch/PR/CI/merge. Docs-only; WF-01 git-wrapper exemption applies to the producer steps, ORCH still lands via branch+PR (ORCHESTRATOR.md s10 note).

task.description:
